question: to the Commission Giuseppe Antoci (The Left) Subject:

The fruit and vegetable market in Vittoria (Sicily) is one of the main European hubs for the marketing of fruit and vegetables and plays a strategic role for the EU’s agri-food sectors. Over the years, investigative and judicial activities have highlighted the risk of organised crime infiltrating the fruit and vegetable sector, transport and logistics. Recent information has also highlighted the possible use of commercial and logistical networks related to this hub for transnational illicit trafficking, including drug trafficking1. In the light of the European Union’s objective of combating organised crime and protecting the integrity of the internal market and EU financial interests: 1.

Is the Commission aware of the risks of organised crime infiltrating the main European agri-food hubs, with particular reference to the Vittoria market, and does it consider it appropriate to assess the impact on the internal market?

Does it consider the monitoring tools and conditionality instruments to be up to the job of ensuring EU funds, in particular those under the common agricultural policy and cohesion policy, are not paid out to businesses affected by disqualifications or infiltrated by organised crime?

Will it consider taking further EU initiatives to prevent this infiltration, by strengthening cooperation between the Member States, Europol, Eurojust and the European Public Prosecutor’s Office and checks on the traceability of supply chains and the security of commercial logistics?

If these risks materialised, there would be serious consequences for competition, the protection of honest economic operators, the safety of agri-food chains and the protection of the EU’s financial interests. 1
